gp.heading: Cost of Revenue and Gross Margin
gp.text:
Cost of revenue for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 consisted primarily of direct labor costs; amortization of certain acquired intangible assets and software development costs; outsourced authentication service costs; and other costs attributable to the provision of service offerings.

Cost of revenue for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025 consisted primarily of the cost of direct labor and cloud service costs.

The increase in gross profit was attributable to higher revenue in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. Our gross margin can be affected by a number of factors, primarily including changes in average selling price and foreign exchange rates, as well as fluctuations in our cost of revenue due to changes in labor costs, outsourced authentication service costs and cloud service costs.

The following table presents revenues and gross margin, for the periods indicated:

Gross margin decreased to 73.6% and 76.3% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, from 85.0% and 83.0% for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The decrease primarily reflected higher amortization costs included in cost of revenues.

rd.heading: Research and Development
rd.text:
Research and development expenses consist primarily of personnel expenses, payments to suppliers for design services, safety and regulatory testing, product certification expenditures to qualify our products for sale into specific markets, prototypes, IT, and other consulting fees. Research and development expenses are recognized as they are incurred. Our research and development organization is focused on enhancing our ability to introduce innovative and easy-to-use products and services. The following table presents research and development expenses for the periods indicated:

Research and development expenses increased by $44 thousand and $72 thousand in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The increase primarily reflects ongoing enhancements and optimizations to our system during the respective periods.

Research and development expenses may fluctuate depending on the timing and number of development activities and could vary significantly as a percentage of revenues, depending on actual revenues achieved in any given year.

sm.heading: Selling and Marketing
sm.text:
Selling and marketing expenses consist primarily of business promotion and corporate publicity expenses. The following table presents selling and marketing expenses for the periods indicated:

Selling and marketing expenses increased by $139 thousand and $409 thousand in the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively, primarily due to the Company’s business transformation and stock-based compensation expenses in connection with equity awards granted in May 2026 under the 2025 Plan. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, selling and marketing expenses primarily reflected costs related to the expansion of our four core business lines– SaaS- MCN digital services, software services, phygital art advisory services, and other services – as well as corporate branding initiatives.

For the remainder of fiscal 2026, we expect selling and marketing expenses to fluctuate with sales levels because certain expenses, such as commissions, are determined based on revenue. Forecasting selling and marketing expenses is highly dependent on expected revenue levels, and actual expenses could vary significantly with actual revenue achieved in any given quarter. Marketing expenses may also fluctuate depending on the timing, extent and nature of marketing programs.

ga.heading: General and Administrative
ga.text:
General and administrative expenses consist of salaries and related expenses for executives, finance and accounting, human resources, information technology (“IT”), professional fees, facility allocations, and other general corporate expenses. The following table presents general and administrative expenses, for the periods indicated:

General and administrative expenses decreased by $756 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared with the three months ended September 30, 2025 and increased by $235 thousand for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared with the nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The quarterly decrease primarily reflected the absence of the prior-year warrant compensation expense. The nine-month increase primarily reflected higher share-based compensation expense, legal and audit fees, and other fees.

Future general and administrative expense increases or decreases in absolute dollars are difficult to predict because certain costs are hard to forecast.

da_op.text: Cash provided by operating activities of $2.5 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2025 reflected our net loss of $1.3 million, adjusted for non-cash expenses, consisting primarily of $1.1 million in issuance of warrants for service, $225 thousand in depreciation and amortization expense and $77 thousand in stock-based compensation. Uses of cash included an increase in other receivables of $431 thousand. Sources of cash included an increase of contract liabilities of $2.5 million.

prov.text: The Company recognized deferred tax assets of $27,102 as of September 30, 2026, which arose primarily from the allowance for credit losses on other receivables.

nonop.text: Our historical cash outflows have primarily been associated with: (1) cash used for operating activities such as personnel costs, cost of services, general office expenses, professional service fees, and other working capital needs; (2) cash used for research and development and sales and marketing initiatives; (3) capital expenditures related to the acquisition of property, equipment and software; (4) cash used to repay our debt obligations and related interest expense; and (5) cash used for acquisitions. Fluctuations in our working capital due to timing differences of our cash receipts and cash disbursements also impact our cash inflows and outflows.

net.text: Cash provided by operating activities of $2.5 million during the nine months ended September 30, 2025 reflected our net loss of $1.3 million, adjusted for non-cash expenses, consisting primarily of $1.1 million in issuance of warrants for service, $225 thousand in depreciation and amortization expense and $77 thousand in stock-based compensation. Uses of cash included an increase in other receivables of $431 thousand. Sources of cash included an increase of contract liabilities of $2.5 million.

ocf.text: Cash Flows from Operating Activities. Cash used for operating activities was $13 thousand for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared with net income of $3.6 million. Noncash adjustments included $1.0 million of depreciation and amortization, $767 thousand of stock-based compensation and $150 thousand of amortization of deferred financing costs. Operating-asset and liability changes included a $5.8 million increase in accounts receivable and decreases of $1.4 million in contract liabilities and $352 thousand in income tax payable, partially offset by a $462 thousand decrease in other receivables and increases of $571 thousand in accrued expenses and other current liabilities and $1.0 million in accounts payable. These adjustments are not necessarily cash receipts or payments in the amounts of the related balance changes. The introduction of post-paid arrangements for MCN digital services and phygital art advisory services in the second quarter of 2026 changed the timing of collections relative to service delivery. Customers under those arrangements are granted payment terms of 90 days from the contract signing date. The Company continues to monitor collectability. The cash outflow related to operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was primarily due to a security deposit for artworks and slower collection of accounts receivable.

net sales.heading: Revenues
net sales.text:
Our revenues increased by $0.7 million and $7.6 million for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, respectively. The increase in revenues primarily reflects the Company’s strategic transition from legacy hardware operations to SaaS solutions, with a new business model focusing on integrating AI and big data into content creation and brand management, and the successful expansion into multiple new business lines, including SaaS - MCN digital services, software services, phygital art advisory services (currently, digital authentication services), and other services, most of which experienced rapid growth following their launch. Notably, during March 2025, we successfully secured our first customer orders and generated initial sales, marking a critical milestone in the strategic pivot. Our target clients are individuals or entities seeking to grow their online presence as influencers or content creators, enterprises requiring customized software solutions, art owners and institutions in need of phygital art advisory services, and participants in the music industry.

For our SaaS - MCN digital services, as of September 30, 2026, we onboarded 939 customers, representing total service fees of $9.2 million, of which $9.0 million has been recognized as revenue cumulatively.

intro.text: FiEE, Inc. (NASDAQ:FIEE), formerly Minim, Inc., was founded in 1977. The Company has a historical track record of delivering comprehensive WiFi/Software as a Service platform in the market. After years of development, FiEE made the strategic decision to transition to a Software First Model in 2024 to expand its technology portfolio and revenue streams. In 2025, FiEE rebranded itself as a technology company leveraging its expertise in IoT, connectivity, and AI to explore new business prospects and extend its global footprint. FiEE’s services are structured into four key categories: Cloud-Managed Connectivity (WiFi) Platform, IoT Hardware Sales & Licensing, SaaS Solutions, and Professional To-C and To-B Services & Support.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
